query: Which deterministic fields and probabilistic matching weights/thresholds will we use to link lab-error events to clinical outcomes, and how will we validate linkage accuracy against a gold standard?

response.query: Which deterministic fields and probabilistic matching weights/thresholds will we use to link lab-error events to clinical outcomes, and how will we validate linkage accuracy against a gold standard?
response.answer: We will use deterministic fields like patient ID and lab timestamps, and probabilistic matching weights based on clinical outcome codes. Validation will use a gold standard of manually verified cases.

results.title: Is it 3 years, or 3 decades away? Disagreements on AGI timelines
results.content: I’m not actually sure, but it’s plausible that I have the most aggressive timelines out of people at Epoch. So it’s like, with a caveat that I’m not sure what he exactly is trying to imply by those developments, it could just be some sort of like, narrow system that is very good at understanding science and integrating scientific papers or something. I think if you think about like that, I would maybe say more than 30 years or something. And so then if you think about that, if I said, what is my median timeline to 30% GDP growth, then I would have to take into account both my timeline to that particular capability, but also the fact that even at that level of capability, I’m only maybe 70, 80% sure that would lead to such rapid growth, which I think leads naturally to like 20 year timelines or median timelines, or maybe even slightly longer than 20 years. But I think if you just focus on capabilities, like the capabilities that people are sufficient to reaching that level of growth, then my median is more like 10 to 15 or maybe even shorter than that.
